scope: independent root audit of the target-retaining gcd carrier, safe saturation, chart partition, rejected-mass identity, capacity arithmetic, ambient countermodels, dependencies, and replay

checks.root_repairs: Canonicalized output paths and replay instructions. No mathematical repair was required.

mathematical_audit.exact_carrier: On the triple-minor chart p divides Pi_r, and Item334 says an original collision is exactly simultaneous vanishing of T0 and T1. Unit denominators therefore make p|gcd(Pi_r,|num T0|,|num T1|) equivalent to the actual degenerate collision.
mathematical_audit.saturation: Item338 gives p not dividing S_(r,s). Removing full prime powers supported by S preserves tied-p divisibility, and the operation is monotone under divisibility, so Gamma_sat divides Pi_sat.
mathematical_audit.internal_branches: When f is nonzero, triple-minor vanishing puts b and v on its line and leaves one localized target scalar. When f is zero, collinearity of b and v does not fix their proportionality constant, so both coordinates of 9*4^s*b-11*v remain necessary.
mathematical_audit.partition: The ray partitions into the all-minor-zero chart, the ell-nonzero chart, and the remaining ell-zero chart. The old gate forces mu=0 in the last chart; C nonzero then excludes a collision, while C zero returns to the degenerate chart. Hence the stated partition is exact.
mathematical_audit.rejected_mass: Raw ray mass minus collision mass is exactly rejected-degenerate plus rejected-nondegenerate plus automatic-obstruction mass. Therefore the only directly bookable degenerate quantity is D_e-G_e, not either chart mass alone.
mathematical_audit.capacity: Bounds D_e>=dM+o(M) and G_e<=gM+o(M) yield saving max(0,d-g)/6. Alternatively chartwise collision bounds g+n below 1/35 yield saving (1/35-g-n)/6. A complete one-ray reward is 1/210.
mathematical_audit.scope: The finite-field rank-one and primitive-integer packets preserve only the declared minor/support/height information. They are not actual connection values and close no formula-specific moving-divisor theorem.
